alignments.note: The complex frame 'by ... means' wraps discontinuously around the relative, so rule 78 takes it out of rule 67's divided case: a discontinuous wrap riding an expressed proper preposition heads on the prepositional word. The corpus is 39 to 2 for that reading and the Catholic-epistle neighbours are unanimous (1PE.1.20, 1PE.2.13, 1PE.3.14, 1JN.3.8, 2JN.1.2). The frame stays undivided on the preposition under rule 67.
Article precedes its noun, so under rule 31 it takes the determiner and the supplied relativizer, discontinuously, headed on 'the'.
Adverbial predicate carries the supplied copula under rule 53; no verb stands in the clause for it otherwise.
Auxiliary rides with the participle under rule 9; head on the lexical verb.
Dative of means with no determiner, so the case preposition stays with the noun under rules 21 and 23.
